Question B-003-011-003.

Why the correct answer is right: A variable oscillator lets the operator tune within a range instead of being limited to one of the installed crystal frequencies.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Frequency is not constrained to the available crystals": This is the correct choice because a variable oscillator lets the operator tune within a range instead of being limited to one of the installed crystal frequencies.
- sourceIndex 1: "Use of higher speed Morse code is supported": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from Frequency is not constrained to the available crystals. In CW quality, AM sidebands, transmitter efficiency, and oscillator stability, more of that quantity would not address the fault and can make a clean-signal problem worse.
- sourceIndex 2: "Greater suppression of key clicks": This answer would fit a different fault than Frequency is not constrained to the available crystals. In CW quality, AM sidebands, transmitter efficiency, and oscillator stability, key clicks are abrupt keying-edge products, not the frequency or mode concept in this item.
- sourceIndex 3: "Greater suppression of harmonics": This option confuses another station topic with Frequency is not constrained to the available crystals. In CW quality, AM sidebands, transmitter efficiency, and oscillator stability, harmonics are unwanted multiples of the transmit frequency, a different problem from the one being asked about.
